message:
docs(policy): name the two completions, and say where automation stops

Three gaps the review found in e3dca33.

The new "minimise what the user has to do" clause tells the agent to run the tests,
take the screenshots and click the buttons itself, and nothing said where that stops.
Read on its own it permits stopping a host the user is working on. It stops at
isolated test builds, fixtures and temporary profiles; touching a product process the
user is actually using needs explicit approval, and even then a recovery baseline --
process identity, installed file hashes, an installer to go back to -- is recorded
first.

"Complete" meant two things one line apart: the deployment section called eight steps
completion and the next sentence said behaviour the user performs decides completion.
0.2.115 went out through exactly that gap, having passed all eight steps with no
button to press. Deployment completion is now named as the milestone it is, and task
completion runs to the behaviour check.

And the workflow's "after each meaningful task, commit" had hardened into history,
plan and commit for every corrected sentence. Records and commits follow meaningful
units of work.

Three smaller things while here: the dependency tags get one spelling, the swap
failure path is written down (the .tmp files are removed and the previous release
stays published, gnlink_deploy.sh:441-443) so the correction does not read worse than
the script behaves, and the log line at :445 still carries the env-only claim -- noted
as follow-up, not touched, because this is a docs-only change.
